HOW TO SUBMIT PUBLIC COMMENTS:
In Person:
Anyone who desires to address the City Council during
Open Forum
, must complete and file a pink speaker’s card with the City Clerk
prior
to the City Council’s consideration of the item.
Online speakers:
must raise their hand when instructed by the clerk. Once the City Clerk has announced the item and given a count of the number of total speakers, no person shall be permitted to speak on the item other than those persons who have submitted their names to the City Clerk or those that have their hand raised.
The amount of time allotted to individual speakers shall be determined based on the total number of persons requesting to speak during this item. The time allocation for each speaker will be as follows: 15 or fewer speakers, a maximum of 2 minutes; 16 to 24 speakers, a maximum of 1 and one-half minutes; and 25 or more speakers, a maximum of 1 minute.
NON-PUBLIC HEARING ITEMS LISTED ON THE AGENDA: Each speaker will be allowed up to TWO minutes to address the Council.  PUBLIC HEARING ITEMS: Speakers are allowed up to THREE (3) minutes to address the Council.

Procedures for Removing Items from the Consent Calendar
:
Members of the public who request to remove an item from the consent calendar must first discuss the item with a staff member by phone or a back-and-forth email discussion, and state the name of the staff member when requesting removal of the item from the consent calendar
(by 2 p.m. the day of the meeting)
.  The procedures for discussion do not apply to items sponsored by the mayor or councilmembers.
Any member of the City Council who would like to remove an item from the consent calendar must notify the appropriate staff person and the City Clerk’s Office prior to the meeting. Although members of the City Council are encouraged to ask questions and share concerns with staff ahead of the meeting, they are not required to do so.
The Clerk’s Office must be informed of any requests to remove items from the Consent Calendar. Items removed from the Consent Calendar shall be placed at the end of the agenda for consideration.
CONDUCT AT MEETINGS:
Richmond City Council meetings are limited public forums during which the City strives to provide an open, safe atmosphere and promote robust public debate. Members of the public, however, must comply with state law, as well as the City’s laws and procedures and may not actually disrupt the orderly conduct of these meetings. The public, for example, may not shout or use amplifying devices, must submit comment cards and speak during their allotted time, may not create a physical disturbance, may not speak on matters unrelated to issues within the jurisdiction of the City Council or the agenda item at hand, and may not cause immediate threats to public safety.
Click here for City Harassment Policy
Accessibility for Individuals with Disabilities:
Upon request, the City will provide for written agenda materials in appropriate alternative formats, or disability-related modification or accommodation, including auxiliary aids or services and sign language interpreters, to enable individuals with disabilities to participate in and provide comments at/related to public meetings. Please submit a request, including your name, phone number and/or email address, and a description of the modification, accommodation, auxiliary aid, service or alternative format requested at least two days before the meeting.  Requests should be emailed to
[email protected]
or submitted by phone at 510-620-6513, ext. 9, or 510-620-6509.  Requests made by mail to City Clerk’s Office, City Council meeting, 450 Civic Center Plaza, Richmond, CA 94804 must be received at least two days before the meeting. Requests will be granted whenever possible and resolved in favor of accessibility.
Unless otherwise noted in an agenda description, all actions taken by the Council include a determination that CEQA does not apply (i.e., the action is not a project and therefore exempt from CEQA).
Disclaimer:  The City Clerk's Office translates agendas to enhance public access.  Translated agendas are provided as a courtesy and do not constitute legal notice of the meeting or items to be discussed.  In case of discrepancy, the English agenda will prevail.

Claudia Citroen
Councilmember Jimenez, as you are well aware, continues to disregard established Council procedures by advancing personal and political priorities ahead of urgent matters affecting Richmond residents. This repeated pattern reflects misplaced priorities, poor governance, and a troubling lack of accountability.

The Mayor's own public admission—"Oh, I must not have read the consent calendar item carefully enough"—after I questioned why the Rent Board continues to receive General Fund support despite voters approving a financially self-sustaining Rent Board, should concern every resident. Such an admission demonstrates inadequate review of agenda materials before public votes are cast.

Equally concerning, after I timely exercised my right under Council procedures to pull the item from the consent calendar for public discussion, it was later returned to the consent calendar over my objection. That decision diminished transparency, limited meaningful public deliberation, and weakened public confidence in the integrity of the Council's decision-making process.

Consent calendars exist to expedite routine, noncontroversial administrative matters—not to minimize public discussion of significant policy or funding decisions. When a Councilmember or member of the public timely requests that an item receive separate consideration, the spirit of transparent government requires that the matter be fully discussed in open session rather than returned to the consent calendar in a manner that appears to limit public participation.

This is not an isolated incident. Time and again, this Council delays or sidelines urgent matters involving public safety, staffing shortages, infrastructure maintenance, fiscal oversight, and core municipal services while devoting substantial time and public resources to discretionary initiatives. Richmond residents expect their elected officials to address essential government functions before advancing ideological or special-interest priorities.

Good governance requires diligent review of agenda items, respect for established procedures, transparent deliberation, meaningful public participation, and responsible stewardship of taxpayer funds. Public confidence depends upon informed decision-making. When elected officials acknowledge they have not carefully reviewed agenda items before voting, it raises legitimate concerns regarding oversight, fiscal accountability, and the integrity of the legislative process.

Procedural rules should be applied consistently and fairly. Residents who comply with established Council procedures should not reasonably perceive that those procedures can be circumvented in ways that reduce transparency or meaningful public review. At a time when the City continues to face staffing shortages, infrastructure demands, and competing budget priorities, taxpayers deserve careful scrutiny of every discretionary expenditure and every significant policy decision.

I respectfully request that significant policy and funding decisions be removed from the consent calendar and scheduled under regular business for full public discussion. Those items should be accompanied by complete fiscal analyses, clear legal authority, and sufficient supporting documentation to allow both the Council and the public to make informed decisions.

Transparency, accountability, and public trust are not procedural formalities—they are fundamental obligations of representative government. Richmond residents deserve a Council that places public safety, fiscal responsibility, operational efficiency, and open government ahead of politics and expediency. It is time to restore public confidence by respecting established procedures, engaging in meaningful public deliberation, and ensuring that every significant decision receives the careful review it deserves.
APPOINT the mayor, vice mayor, city attorney, city clerk, and city manager to an ad hoc committee to develop proposed amendments to the City Council Rules of Procedure and Order, along with other operational refinements, to bring forward to the full City Council for approval within 60 days of its formation – Mayor’s Office (Mayor Eduardo Martinez 510-620-6502).

agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: Richmond Council to support California bill tightening CEQA exemptions
agenda_briefs.summary: Council is set to vote on a resolution to support California Senate Bill 954, which would tighten exemptions under the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA). The bill would require advanced manufacturing projects to have zero-emission backup generation, be sited in heavy industrial zones with 1,600-foot setbacks from sensitive receptors and 1,000-foot setbacks from disadvantaged communities, not harm tribal resources, and include a community benefits agreement and high roads labor standards. This is a proposed decision and has not yet been approved.
